- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.2) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to capture mean reversion.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak for 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment shifts from neutral to bullish, model often fails to adjust quickly; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to match sentiment momentum.  
- In low-sentiment periods (≤0.3), model tends to underestimate; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for hidden volatility.  
- Model consistently underestimates in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.7); apply a 1–2% upward bias for 7–14 days.  
- If recent history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model often fails to correct; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to counteract.
